IPT.evidence_source: [/page/2/Text/1] Interpersonal psychotherapy is a time-limited psychotherapy that focuses on current problems. The procedures are specified in a manual.27 The goals of IPT-A are to reduce depressive symptoms and improve interpersonal functioning by relating the symptoms to 1 or more of 4 problem areas (grief, role disputes, role transitions, and interpersonal deficits) and by developing strategies for dealing with these problems.28 Two independent studies have demonstrated the efficacy of IPT-A.17,18 The IPT-A intervention was delivered as 12 sessions during a 12- to 16-week period.
